utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I would now merely avail myself of the opportunity to ask Mr. Vujin, who I believe is now present, whether he would consent to a replacement judge being appointed in the contempt matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: I think it's probably appropriate for my co-counsel to leave at this stage, I think, technically. I think Mr. Keegan is nodding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: No objections whatever from the bench? I just thought that it might be physically possible for you to remain.

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: I will certainly remain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: No, it's not required at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You're fully at liberty to make your exit at this point. Yes. I'm reminded by Mr. Hocking that it would be appropriate for us to invite in Mr. Abell as well. Mr. Clegg, you’re quite free to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: Along with Mr. Livingston, I thought. Probably he would want to leave, but I'm prepared to stay out of interest --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Is Mr. Livingston with you?

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then he also has permission to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: We're glad to see Mr. Vujin and Mr. Domazet. We are awaiting the presence of Mr. Abell. Mr. Vujin, Mr. Domazet, the bench is a little truncate this afternoon. Unfortunately, one of our members, Judge Wang, is not well and this accounts for the shape of the bench this afternoon. It also accounts for the rather informal ways, in many respects, in which we have been proceeding this afternoon. We've come now -- it's half past three -- to the matter in which Mr. Vujin is involved, and the position is that we find that we cannot proceed because of the absence of Judge Wang. The President, with whom we have spoken, is willing to appoint a replacement Judge to continue with the case but that would require the consent of parties, we think, or at least it would be prudent to obtain the consent of the parties. There are no parties stricto sensu, except perhaps in the case of Mr. Vujin. Mr. Vujin, in your absence and because of the informal nature of the course which the proceedings have taken, we have obtained the consent of Mr. Abell, speaking on behalf of Mr. Tadic, and of the Prosecution to a replacement Judge being appointed in the case in which you are involved, but the President cannot proceed to do so without the consent of all parties. So we're asking whether you would also consent to that being done.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. You have my agreement on that. Yes, Your Honour, you do have my agreement. I consent to the replacement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Vujin, I did not have the mechanism properly adjusted, and so I did not hear correctly what you said, but I'm reading it off the transcript. You have expressed your agreement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will report accordingly to the President. We will suggest this course, that the Court meets tomorrow, hopefully with a replacement judge, at a time which I will indicate to you in a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I have conferred with my colleagues on the bench, and I propose that we assemble at 10.00 in the morning. Mr. Clegg?

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: As all parties are here in the contempt hearing, can I merely raise the question of the motion that I have made in relation to those proceedings and ask whether it be convenient to deal with that hopefully at 10.00 tomorrow morning? I don't think it can be dealt with by the four judges today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. That's a motion in the contempt matter --

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: -- or in the appeal matter proper?

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: I'm afraid I get the dividing line between the two a bit confused. It's a motion that affects the presence of Witness D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You want a certain witness to be present in court?

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: So it seems to me that that is a matter that ought to be decided in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You would like to have that discussed in the morning at 10.00?

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The Chamber is agreeable.

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: If there is no other business, the Chamber will now stand adjourned until 10.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: 3.34 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 31st day of August, 1999, at 10 a.m.
